correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts \(p^3\) and \(p^2q\). For cubes, the exact condition is \(16\mid2p^3+p+1\), which for odd primes is equivalent to \(p\equiv5\pmod{16}\), while \(p=2\) fails. For \(p^2q\), the exact condition \(36\mid q(2p^2+1)+2p+1\) is split completely by the exceptional primes \(2,3\) and by residues modulo \(3\), \(4\), and \(9\). The three surviving branches are necessary and sufficient.
